text: A song of ascents. In my distress I called to the LORD, and he answered me.
Deliver me, LORD, from lying lips, from a deceitful tongue.
What will he give you, and what more will he add to you, you deceitful tongue?

versions.text: What will he do to you, and what more besides, you deceitful tongue?
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verbs are נתן (give) and יסף (add), a fixed oath-like formula of retribution. The clipped phrase "and what more besides" leaves the clause without a verb and reads awkwardly aloud; restoring the parallel verbs gives a fuller, more rhythmic line and keeps closer to the Hebrew.

text: Sharpened arrows of a warrior, and glowing coals of the broom bush!

versions.text: A warrior's sharpened arrows, and burning coals of the broom bush.
versions.explanation: This verse is the answer to the question in verse 3, so an exclamation point helps the oral reader hear the connection. "Sharpened arrows of a warrior" also keeps the Hebrew word order and its stronger rhythm, and "glowing coals" better renders גַּחֲלֵי (embers already burning). A footnote could note that broom-wood charcoal was prized for burning long and fiercely.

text: How miserable I am, living as a stranger in Meshech, dwelling among the tents of Kedar!
Too long have I lived among those who hate peace.
I am for peace, but when I speak, they are for war.
